whyThisShow: This is the last night of what one listener called "The Honey Year" — the run of shows from late 1973 into early 1974 where Jerry's guitar ran clean and warm, barely touched by distortion pedals. The Wall of Sound debuted at the very next show on March 23rd, so this Winterland date sits at a genuine hinge point in the band's evolution. One reviewer did flag that some listeners find the pace too restrained, so if you need the Dead at full throttle this may not be your first stop. But for heads who love the laid-back, jazzy side of the band, this whole February Winterland run is regarded as essential, and the 24th is one of its peaks.
listenFor: The China Cat > Rider transition is a particular standout — the UJB-like segue jam drew one reviewer to call it "the best ever UJB-like segue jam" of that entire era, noting that "Jerry's tone is just crystal clear and in your face". The Jack Straw also drew specific attention, described as one of the top five ever with licks that are "so f-ing smooth". Row Jimmy stood out to one listener as "really slowed down and almost reggae like" with notable slide guitar work from Jerry. The Morning Dew closes the main set and is the performance that prompted one reviewer's most intense praise — they recommend listening with the volume high to catch the moments where Jerry "fizzles the notes away" at the end.
context: Recorded at Winterland Arena in San Francisco on February 24, 1974, this show falls squarely in the wall-of-sound era, though the Wall of Sound PA system itself had not yet been deployed — that happened at the next show on March 23rd. The recording circulates as a soundboard (identifier: gd74-02-24.sbd.windsor.199.sbefail.shnf) and was officially released as Dave's Picks Vol. 13. One reviewer rated it "the best sound quality for any 1974 show on this archive". The show is part of a celebrated Winterland run that included February 22nd and 23rd, all of which reviewers recommend getting together.
funFact: One listener described a recurring out-of-body experience while playing the Morning Dew in the dark with a candle lit, writing that their "spirit and soul is litterally transported back to 1974" and that they can "feel the energy" of Winterland — and specifically notes this happened "without LSD".
headline: Last night of the honey year, Winterland, February '74.
